scope: Rebuild the Jade corner teahouse completely as a neon cyberpunk shopfront
Replace the traditional tiled pitch with a flat machine roof after the user rejected it

rooftopPlant: three packaged condensers on a bolted cranked base
horizontal water tank on anchor-bolted cradles
braced tapered antenna mast with dish and equipment cabinet
kitchen extract on a curb with grease filter and rain hood
curbed access hatch with fixed ladder
geometry.daylightValueCheck: Cladding luminance raised from 0.057 to 0.129 so the shop no longer reads as the darkest mass in the district at midday (tenement 0.115, toyshop 0.199, cinema 0.224, paving 0.287)

additionalChecks: Every aperture is a through-hole, probed by ray in the authored scene
Hollow manifold envelope with one connected component
The removed tiled pitch, gables and ridge sign cannot return
Roof deck stays level and carries no diagonal smoothed shading
Coping caps the parapet at its finished level
Approach paving stays flush and supported on all four sides
Interior bounce covers ceiling, floor and both walls
The fitted night channel clears the parapet face and stays below the coping

validation.npmBuild: passed; existing large JS chunk advisory

browserReview: Night front: the cyan coping line and the rooftop JADE board read against the dark deck; the condenser bank, tank, cabinet and mast silhouette above the shopfront neon
Day front: standing seams, belt fixings, coping, extract hood, tank, hatch and ladder all read as fitted plant on a ribbed deck
Night side: the east service run reads as fitted equipment below the parapet light line
Day rear: the flank keeps its belt, trims, downpipe and drip, and the plant reads over the coping
fixedDuringQA: Solid envelope produced shallow recesses instead of through-apertures; added a room void cutter
Door surrounds dropped 30 mm below paving; gave door bays a shallow sill instead of the window sill
Table pedestal and interior services sat below the floor level
Shop interior was unlit surfaces behind glass; added one broad interior ceiling emitter and removed the redundant side-door emitter
Dark-on-dark service door, shutter laths and pipes were invisible in daylight; switched them to contrasting metal finishes
Rear elevation had no belt course; extended it around all four elevations
Ridge cabinet was single-sided; named both faces
Roof deck planarity check tripped on its own bevel band; the check now reads evaluated corner normals
Coping drip ring was named inconsistently with the rest of the roof set

Daylight review: the rebuilt teahouse was the darkest mass in a bright pastel scene, so its pressed-metal cladding was lifted from #3b4453 to #5c6577 and its interior emitter's daytime share reduced from 40% to 25%
